title: Your Fitness New Year's Resolution will fail. Here's why
summary: NH gives five reasons fitness resolutions fail: waiting for January 1, relying on motivation, going too hard, having no real purpose, and setting impossible deadlines or chasing perfection. He tells viewers to turn resolutions into discipline and make lifting a lifelong habit.
claims: Waiting until January 1 to start is conformism; if you needed everyone else to start, you will quit when they do
Most people enjoy making a resolution more than carrying it out
Don't wait for a date to change your life; start now
Lifting is mostly done alone; you can't count on others cheering you on
Gyms are packed on January 1 and empty again by February
Motivation is a short-lived high; build discipline through routine and habit so you still train when motivation is gone
After 10 years of lifting he is often unmotivated, for example training in a 20-degree garage after a 10-hour shift, but he goes because it is scheduled
Going all-out for one month loses to steady training for 12 months; even someone who lasts 2 months beats you by simply showing up
People who train hard every January and then skip 11 months look the same all year
Beginners should lower intensity and training volume at first so the habit lasts
Make it a game to be the last one standing at your gym, outlasting the January crowd
Set a real purpose, even a modest one like 20 push-ups, then move on to the next goal
Many resolutions are borrowed from fads or other people; the gym may not suit you and swimming or tennis are valid
It took him years to realise pure bodybuilding was his calling
Goals and deadlines are different; avoid deadlines, because an impossible one such as looking like Arnold in 6 months means you never really try
Setting deadlines implies you expect to stop; lifting is for life
Chasing the perfect workout or perfect conditions leads to doing nothing
Turn the resolution into dedication and motivation into discipline
exercises: example of a modest beginner goal of 20 reps
